args.content:
Working definition: The 'house tier' is the customer tier (memory.bench.customers.tier) that placed the most orders. Operationally: join memory.bench.orders to memory.bench.customers on customer_id, GROUP BY tier, COUNT(order_id) (or COUNT(*)) per tier, and the house tier is the tier with the highest order count, e.g.:
SELECT c.tier, COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM memory.bench.orders o
JOIN memory.bench.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.tier
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
This is a derived business definition, not a stored column, and should be recomputed from current order volume by tier whenever asked.
